title: Glide Review 2026: Features, Pros, and Cons
summary: Glide is the easiest no-code app builder to get started with. The thing to understand before committing is that Glide Classic and GlideOS are now separate products with separate pricing and no migration path.
body_markdown:
*Reviewed September 26, 2026. This is a research-based review of Glide's official pricing and published customer feedback — not a hands-on benchmark. Jet Admin publishes this comparison and is a competing product; competitor strengths are stated as found.*


Glide is worth considering when you want a working app from a spreadsheet faster than any comparable tool allows, and your design requirements are modest. Its strongest advantage is how little there is to learn. The trade-off is a hard one to spot from the outside: **Glide Classic and GlideOS are now separate products** , on separate subscriptions, with no migration path between them — so "Glide" means two different purchases depending on which you sign up for.


This review covers that split first, then what Glide does well, its real limits, what reviewers report and how it compares with Jet Admin.


## Glide review: the quick verdict


Glide suits small teams that need a shared operational app quickly, especially on data already in a spreadsheet, and can accept the platform's design ceiling. It is a weaker fit for brand-critical interfaces, native mobile distribution, or teams needing many collaborators.


Strong reasons to consider Glide Trade-offs to evaluate


Minimal learning curve — real apps in hours Glide Classic and GlideOS are separate products with no migration path


Excellent spreadsheet-to-app workflow Limited design and branding control


Strong template library and built-in integrations Team members are tightly capped per plan (2 / 2 / 3 / 5+)


Very high ratings from Glide Classic reviewers No native app-store publishing or push notifications


No numerical score is given, because we did not run a scored hands-on evaluation.


## What is Glide? (And which Glide?)


Glide builds apps from structured data — classically a Google Sheet — with a drag-and-drop editor and no code. You connect a data source, choose layouts, set visibility rules and share the result.


**The distinction that matters most in 2026:** Glide has launched GlideOS as a standalone AI platform on its own subscription. It does not share data or pricing with Glide Classic, and there is no migration path between them.


That has a practical consequence for anyone researching Glide. Most of the glowing review history — including a 4.7 rating across 818 G2 reviews — was earned by Glide Classic. The pricing published today describes GlideOS. Those are not the same product, and you should establish which one you are evaluating before reading anything else about it, including the sections below.


The pricing table in this review is GlideOS. The customer feedback is predominantly Glide Classic. We have flagged that separation rather than blending them.


## Glide's key features


### 1. Spreadsheet to app, genuinely quickly


Connect a Google Sheet and Glide produces a usable app structure from it. Reviewers consistently describe building functional apps in hours.


For a team already running a process in a spreadsheet, this is the shortest path to something with logins and role-appropriate views. It is the clearest reason to choose Glide over a more capable but slower platform.


### 2. A drag-and-drop editor with a low floor


The editor is repeatedly described as simple, intuitive and user-friendly, with a minimal learning curve. Compared with platforms where reviewers measure the learning investment in months, this is a genuine differentiator for non-technical builders.


### 3. Templates and built-in integrations


A template directory and built-in integrations mean most common patterns — directories, trackers, request forms, internal catalogues — start from something rather than nothing.


### 4. Workflows and AI features, gated by plan


On GlideOS, enabled workflows are capped per tier: one on Basic, five on Plus, unlimited on Pro. AI features and agent mode selection unlock at Basic, custom agent building via MCP at Pro.


Check this ladder against your actual automation needs, because one enabled workflow is a real constraint for an operational app.


### 5. Publishing scope changes by plan


Personal and team app publishing unlocks at Basic; *public* app publishing requires Plus. If your app is for customers rather than colleagues, that moves your entry price from $25 to $50 a month before any other consideration.


## Glide pros


### The lowest barrier to a working app in its category


Minimal learning curve plus a genuinely intuitive editor is a rare combination, and reviewers report iterating through design ideas quickly. For teams that have failed to adopt a more powerful tool, Glide's approachability is the feature that matters.


### The Google Sheets path is excellent


If your process already lives in a spreadsheet, Glide turns it into an app with permissions and views without a data migration project. That is a legitimate, cheap answer for a large number of small operational problems.


### Glide Classic earned very strong reviews


A 4.7 rating across 818 G2 reviews is a substantial, positive sample. It reflects real satisfaction with the classic product and should not be dismissed — only correctly attributed.


### Predictable, capped usage


GlideOS plans include defined credit allowances rather than open-ended metering. For buyers who prefer a known monthly number to a usage bill that can surprise them, that is a point in Glide's favour.


## Glide cons and limitations


### The two-product split is the biggest risk


GlideOS and Glide Classic are separate subscriptions that do not share data, and there is no migration path between them.


**Who it affects:** anyone building today who expects to move to the platform's future. **What to do:** ask Glide directly which product your use case belongs in, whether the other will continue to be developed, and what happens if you need to move. Building extensively in the wrong one means rebuilding, not upgrading.


### Design and branding control are limited


Reviewers report that Glide does not let you change everything about how an app looks, making exact brand matching difficult, with multi-action buttons and precise layout positioning missing.


**Who it affects:** customer-facing apps where presentation is part of the product. **What to do:** build one screen to your brand guidelines during a trial. This limit is immediately visible and easy to test.


### Team members are tightly capped


GlideOS includes 2 team members on Free and Basic, 3 on Plus, and Pro starts at 5 with 50 credits included per member.


**Who it affects:** any team where more than a couple of people build or administer. **What to do:** count your builders before choosing a tier — this ladder, not the credit allowance, is what most often forces the upgrade.


### No native app-store publishing or push notifications


Reviewers note the absence of native App Store and Google Play publishing and of native push notifications, alongside data and performance bottlenecks for power users.


**What to evaluate:** if you need a genuine mobile app in a store, Glide does not deliver that. Confirm whether a web app added to a phone's home screen is acceptable to your users before proceeding.


### Pricing communication has drawn criticism


The main community frustration reported is not product quality but pricing communication, with multiple price changes documented in a short period. Trustpilot sits under 2.4 — "Poor" — against G2's 4.7, and that gap is largely about commercial experience rather than capability.


## What do Glide users say?


Source Rating Reviews behind it Which product


[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/glide-2023-07-10/reviews) 4.7 / 5 818 Glide Classic


G2 + Capterra sample 4.0 / 5 15 (14 would recommend) Mixed


Trustpilot Under 2.4 ("Poor") Not verified Mixed


**Positive themes:** minimal learning curve; fast iteration; Google Sheets integration; template directory; straightforward setup.


**Negative themes:** constrained customisation and UI freedom; no native store publishing or push notifications; performance ceilings for power users; pricing changes and how they were communicated.


The honest summary is that people like using Glide and have been less happy with how it is sold. Those are separable concerns, and only one of them is about whether the product will do your job.

### When Glide is the better choice


For a small team with a spreadsheet and a simple operational need, Glide will get there faster and with less learning than almost anything else — including Jet Admin. If that describes you, its approachability is the right reason to pick it.


## Who should use Glide — and who should compare alternatives?


**Good fit:** spreadsheet-backed internal apps; teams of two or three builders; simple directories, trackers and request flows; anyone who needs something working this week.


**Compare alternatives if:** your data belongs in a real database; more than a few people need to build; your brand requires exact design control; you need native mobile distribution; or you are uncomfortable committing to one of two products that cannot migrate to the other.

## Glide review FAQ


### What is Glide?


A no-code platform that builds apps from structured data, classically a Google Sheet, using a drag-and-drop editor with no code required.


### What is the difference between Glide Classic and GlideOS?


They are separate products on separate subscriptions. They do not share data or pricing, and there is no migration path between them. Establish which one you are buying before you build.


### Is Glide free?


GlideOS has a free plan with 2 team members, 10 projects and limited credits. Paid GlideOS tiers begin at $25 per month. Glide Classic is priced separately.


### Can Glide publish a native mobile app?


Reviewers report no native App Store or Google Play publishing and no native push notifications. Confirm whether a web app is sufficient for your users.


### How many people can use a Glide app?


Distinguish builders from users: GlideOS caps team members at 2 on Free and Basic, 3 on Plus and from 5 on Pro. Confirm end-user limits for your specific plan and app type.


### How does Glide compare with Jet Admin?


Glide is fastest for spreadsheet-backed apps built by a couple of people. Jet Admin connects to an existing database or API and includes unlimited users on every plan. The deciding factors are usually where your data lives and how many people need access.


## Establish which Glide you are buying


Before evaluating features or price, ask Glide directly whether your use case belongs in Glide Classic or GlideOS, and what happens if you later need the other. That single question protects you from the one mistake on this platform that cannot be undone by upgrading.


If the answer leaves you uncertain and your data already lives in a database,[build the same app on it with Jet Admin](https://www.jetadmin.io/) and compare both on effort and continuity.
